title: Immortalization of adult human colonic epithelial cells extracted from normal tissues obtained via colonoscopy
protocol: Add 71.48 gm of Hepes to 700 ml of DI water.
Add 10 ml of Phenol Red (1.75 mg/ml) to the mixture.
Adjust pH to 7.0 using Sodium Hydroxide, then add 7.2 gm of glucose, 2.24 gm of potassium chloride, 71.28 gm of sodium chloride, and 1.42 gm of sodium phosphate.
Re-adjust pH to 7.5 and add 300 ml of DI water to complete the volume to 1 liter.
Sterile filter (22 micron filter) the solution and store at 4°C.
Add 13,659 U of collagenase type 1 to 9.1 ml of X media to prepare a 10x stock (final concentration = 1500 U/ml).
Store the collagenase stock for up to 2 weeks in -20°C.
Add 5 mg of dispase to 1.25 ml of X media to prepare a 100x stock (final concentration = 4 mg/ml).
Store the dispase stock for up to 2 weeks in -20°C.
Combine together 3.0 ml of 10x collagenase, 300 μl of 100x dispase, and 750 μl of fetal bovine serum with approximately 26 ml of X media to make a 1x digestion mix (total volume = 30 ml).
Prepare the 1x digestion mix fresh shortly before using it.
Add an appropriate amount of sorbitol to desired volume of X media to prepare a final solution containing 2% sorbitol.
Sterile filter and store the sorbitol-containing media at 4°C.
To 1 L of X media, add EGF.
Add hydrocortisone to the media.
Add insulin to the media.
Add apo-transferrin to the media.
Add sodium selenite to the media.
Add 20 ml of cosmic calf serum to the media.
Do not sterile filter the prepared media.
Keep the media at 4°C.
Place desired amount of media in a vented T75 flask for normoxic tension conditioning.
Place the flask inside a 20% oxygen/7% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Allow the incubator's CO2 to equilibrate with the CO2 within the media for several hours or overnight.
Condition media in plastic containers purged of normal atmospheric air and filled with a gas mixture consisting of 2% oxygen, 7% CO2, and 91% nitrogen.
Seed packaging cells on regular 15 cm dishes and grow in X media supplemented with 10% cosmic calf serum.
Allow cells to become subconfluent.
Exchange packaging cell media for 12 mls of X+2% serum-high EGF media.
Place the packaging cells back into the incubator overnight.
Collect the media using a 10 ml syringe the next day.
Filter the collected media with a 0.45 micron filter.
Use the viral supernatant immediately or store it for up to 6 months at -80°C.
Change growth media to X+ media supplemented with 0.1% serum and 1 ng/ml EGF when cells are 36 hours post-seeding or 50% confluent.
Add 1 µM to 5 µM of the GSK-3beta inhibitor 6-bromoindirubin-3-oxime (BIO) to the media.
Treat cells for 3-5 days with the supplemented media.
Thoroughly mix BIO into the media before adding to cells since the BIO can precipitate out and be toxic to the cells.
Make a mixture of DMSO and cosmic calf serum so that DMSO is 10% of the mixture.
Keep the freezing media always at 4°C.
Treat confluent C26Ci fibroblast cultures with 10 μg/ml of mitomycin C for 2 hours at 37°C.
Seed treated fibroblasts onto Primaria™ plates at a 1:3 split ratio.
Subculture the cells and use them as feeder layers within the next 48 hours.
Obtain biopsies preferably from a patient with minimal stool inside the colon during the procedure.
Place each biopsy in a sterile 15 ml conical tube containing serum-free X media immediately after obtaining.
Maintain the conical tube containing the biopsy and media at 4°C by placing it in an ice-filled container.
Remove X media with a Drummond pipette.
Add 10 ml of ice cold solution A containing 1x antimycotic/antibiotic and 50 μg/ml gentamicin sulfate to biopsies.
Transfer biopsies and SolA-AAG to a new sterile 15 ml conical tube placed horizontally on an ice-filled foam box.
Rock the tube gently for 3 minutes.
Aspirate SolA-AAG and biopsy contents with a 10 ml pipette into a new sterile 15 ml tube.
Let biopsies settle, remove old SolA-AAG, and add fresh SolA-AAG.
Repeat rocking and SolA-AAG exchanges a total of 3 times outside the tissue culture hood.
After the third wash, remove old SolA-AGG and add 5 ml of new SolA-AGG inside the tissue culture vented hood.
Pour intact biopsies in SolA-AGG into a sterile 10 cm normal tissue culture plate sitting on an ice-filled foam box.
Take two sterile standard single-edge razors and mince biopsies to pieces 1 mm or less in size for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the finely minced biopsies with SolA-AAG using a 10 ml pipette attached to a Drummond and deposit into a sterile 15 ml conical tube.
Centrifuge the tube at low g (100-200g) for 4-5 minutes in a conventional tissue culture centrifuge.
Remove and discard the supernatant containing fine debris, leaving only the minced biopsy contents.
Discard the white debris-mucus layer from the top of the minced tissue.
Gently resuspend the remaining minced tissue with new SolA-AAG and transfer to a sterile 15 ml conical tube.
Rock the tube in ice for 3 minutes.
Repeat the centrifugation, washing, and rocking process until the supernatant is clear and minimal amounts of white debris layer remain.
Centrifuge the tube and contents again at low g for 4 minutes.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cleaned minced tissue in 30 ml of 1x digestion mix.
Deposit tissue and digestion mix into a sterile vented T75 flask with a 25 ml pipette.
Set the flask in a 37°C incubator in 20% oxygen / 5% CO2.
Allow minced tissues to break down into individual crypts and clumps of crypts for the next hour.
Collect contents in digestion mix after 1 hr of digestion.
Deposit collected contents into a 50 ml conical tube.
Gently spin the tissues at low g for two minutes.
Change the digestion mix to new mix.
Deposit the new mix and contents back to the 75 vented flask.
Set the incubator for another 1.5 hours.
Check crypts in the second hour of digestion every 15 minutes to avoid over-digestion.
Use a >2mm bore pipette after 2.5 hours of total crypt digestion time.
Draw up and down the crypts in the digest mixture repeatedly (about 50 times).
Break down large clumps of crypts into smaller or individual crypts.
Avoid using small bore pipettes to prevent breaking individual crypts apart.
Stop the digestion once 80% of the digest is composed of individual crypts and small clumps.
Perform a sedimentation step as described by Booth and O'Shea and Evans et al.
Draw 30 mls of digest mixture using a 25ml wide-mouthed pipette, split equally into 50 ml conical tubes.
Add 25 mls of sorbX media to each tube.
Allow the solution to settle for one minute.
Remove the supernatant and transfer it to new 50 ml tubes.
Mix contents then spin down at low g for 2 minutes.
Repeat sedimentation step until the supernatant is clear, performing this process 3 to 4 times.
Resuspend the crypt pellet in normoxia conditioned X+2% serum-high EGF media containing AAG.
Seed crypts into 24 well Primaria plates containing human colonic fibroblast feeder layers.
Pour a volume of media containing crypts not exceeding 500 μl onto each individual well.
Place plates with seeded crypts in a humidified 37°C incubator.
Set incubation conditions to 20% oxygen and 7.5% CO₂.
Maintain undisturbed until the next day.
Seed crypts in X+ media containing 2% serum for optimal attachment.
Use an optimal seeding volume of 500 μl per well.
Perform initial crypt seeding in 20% oxygen to optimize attachment.
Monitor cultures for timing between 21 to 25 days before first passage.
Attach crypts to the Primaria™ surface by 24 hours.
Ensure viable cuboidal cells are adherent to the Primaria™ surface.
Add 0.5 ml of low-oxygen conditioned X+2%-high EGF media containing AAG to each well.
Maintain cells indefinitely in a 2-5% low oxygen environment.
Monitor cell viability within the next 48 to 72 hours for rounding and detachment.
Avoid media changes during this phase.
Take pictures under microscope expeditiously to minimize exposure to ambient conditions.
Add 1 ml of low-oxygen conditioned X+2%-high EGF media containing AAG to each well on Day #5.
Make the total volume in each well 2 mls by adding media.
Initiate explants emergence monitoring on day #6.
Monitor for the appearance of cuboidal cells in explants by day #6 to 12.
Observe mitotic cells within the explants.
Begin serum weaning from day #6 to day #12 to prevent fibroblastic contamination.
Remove antibiotic/antimycotic solution (AAS) from media starting on day #6.
Replace media in all wells with low-oxygen conditioned X+-high EGF medium containing gentamicin and no AAS or serum.
Maintain primary cultures indefinitely from day #1 in the 2-5% oxygen tension.
Change media to low-oxygen conditioned X+-high EGF without serum on day #12.
Wean cells to 0%, 0.5%, 1%, or 2% serum depending on cell health and constitution.
Maintain healthy appearing cells (compact, small size) in as low a serum concentration as possible during the primary culture period.
Perform media changes every 5 days while continuously maintaining cells in 2-5% oxygen tension.
First passage should be performed when cell explants reach 75% confluency.
Wash the explants briefly with warm solution A.
Expose cells to 300 μl of 0.02% EDTA for 3 minutes while continuously moving the plate.
Aspirate the 0.02% EDTA once most feeder layers are removed.
Add 300 μl of trypsin/EDTA solution and incubate for 5 minutes or until explants detach.
Neutralize the trypsin/EDTA with twice its volume in neutralizing solution (600 μl).
Collect cells from wells corresponding to one serum concentration into a 15 ml conical tube.
Top off each tube with 5 ml of solution A and centrifuge at 110 g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the supernatant carefully, leaving a small quantity behind as the pellet may not be visible.
Resuspend cells in low-oxygen conditioned X+ 2% serum-high EGF media.
Choose wells corresponding to healthy explants capable of replication under the lowest serum concentration.
Wait 36 hours after seeding cells from the first passage.
Observe cell division beginning within 36 hours post-seeding, with cuboidal to spindle-shaped morphology.
Maintain cells for a total of 4 to 5 passages in low oxygen conditions using Primaria™ dishes and X+ 2% serum-high EGF media without transduction with Cdk4 and hTERT.
Do not use feeder layers after the first passage when growing cells in serum-supplemented media under low oxygen.
Treat cells with GSK-3Beta inhibitor BIO in reduced serum and EGF concentrations to observe transition to cuboidal morphology.
Observe expression of cytokeratins such as CK18 after treatment with GSK-3Beta inhibitor BIO.
Expect non-immortalized cells to enlarge, cease replication, and fail cell culture tolerance beyond 4 to 5 passages.
Avoid growing cells in media without serum to prevent proliferation beyond 1 to 2 passages.
Recommend expanding a separate batch of non-infected cells during the immortalization process for future use.
Perform viral transduction in an appropriate laminar flow hood using BSL2 containment.
Viral transduction is done when cells are 50% confluent and performed in low oxygen conditions.
Pour 0.5 ml of media containing Cdk4 viral construct harvested from packaging cells into a well of the 6-well dish, with the presence of 0.5x polybrene (2 μg/ml).
Infection takes place over 8 hours; after this period, aspirate and discard the viral supernatant.
Add 3 ml of low-oxygen conditioned X+2% serum-high EGF media to the well post-infection for cell recovery more than 36 hours.
Subculture cells when they reach 85% confluency.
Seed the subcultured cells for antibiotic selection.
Subculture the successfully selected Cdk4-infected cell population in a 1 to 3 ratio into another 6 well Primaria dish when the cells are 80% confluent.
Transduce cells with 0.5 ml of viral supernatant containing the hTERT construct for 8 hours after 36 hours or when the cells reach 50% confluency, in the presence of 0.5x polybrene.
Perform antibiotic selection to isolate the hTERT infected cells previously selected for Cdk4.
Seed 50,000 Cdk4 infected cells into each well of a 6-well Primaria™ dish.
Begin treating cells with G418 forty-eight hours after seeding.
Treat each well with different G418 dosages: 30 μg/ml, 60 μg/ml, 120 μg/ml, 240 μg/ml, and 480 μg/ml, along with a control zero dosage for ten days.
Simultaneously treat control non-infected cells with the same G418 dosage curve as infected cells.
Use the minimum G418 dose that kills all control non-infected cells to select Cdk4 infected cells.
Treat cells with puromycin using dosages of 50 ng/ml, 125 ng/ml, 250 ng/ml, 500 ng/ml, and 1 μg/ml along with a control zero dosage for five days.
Subculture patches of surviving cells once they have grown out sufficiently from the drug concentration that kills non-infected cells.
Transfer subcultured cells to a new Primaria™ plate.
Maintain transduced cells in X+ 2% serum-low EGF media.
Passage Cdk4 and hTERT infected cells when they are 85% confluent.
Seed between 200,000 and 400,000 cells in a 10cm Primaria™ dish.
Alternatively, seed 50,000 cells for a T25 flask or 400,000 cells for a T75 flask.
Change the medium every 3 days.
Freeze back cells every 4 to 5 passages using standard cryovials containing freezing media.
Submerge the cryovials in a "Mr. Frosty" coolie with isopropyl alcohol after seeding.
Store the cells overnight at -80°C before transferring them to a -150°C freezer or liquid nitrogen for long-term storage.
Maintain immortalized cells indefinitely in Primaria™ dishes and in low oxygen conditions.
Check immortalized cells for telomerase activity using standard TRAP assays kits.
Check immortalized cells for Cdk4 activity using western blot methods.
Measure telomere lengths via TRF assays.
Evaluate expression of epithelial proteins using western blots.
Evaluate expression of mesenchymal proteins using western blots.
Perform karyotype analysis initially after immortalization.
Repeat karyotype analysis after long-term culture to evaluate chromosomal abnormalities.
Seed 8000 cells on 13 mm sterile coverslips within a regular 24 well plate.
Rock the plate gently to ensure even cell attachment and settling on coverslip.
Incubate overnight under low-oxygen conditions without disturbing the plates.
Wash cells three times with cold PBS.
Fix cells with a cold 1:1 methanol/acetone solution for 5 minutes or neutral buffered formalin (NBF) for 10 minutes.
Wash fixed cells three times with cold PBS.
Expose fixed cells to cold 0.5% Triton X in PBS over ice for 10 minutes.
Wash cells three times with PBS.
Block with 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS at room temperature on a rocker for 20 minutes.
Remove BSA and wash one time with PBS.
Incubate with primary antibody diluted in PBS for two hours at room temperature or overnight at 4 degrees, using a rocker. Use 300 μl of PBS per well.
Wash cells five times with PBS (2 minutes between washes on a rocker).
Incubate with secondary antibody diluted in PBS for one hour protected from light. Use 300 μl of PBS per well.
Wash cells four times with PBS (2 minutes between washes on a rocker).
Put one drop of DAPI on a glass slide.
Use a bent 27 gauge needle to lift up a coverslip.
Gently clasp the coverslip with forceps and transfer it over the DAPI droplet on the glass slide.
Settle the coverslip face-down over the DAPI droplet.
Use nail polish to fasten the coverslip to the glass slide.
Use positive controls such as colon cancer epithelial cells (e.g., CaCo2 cells) for IF staining.
Use negative controls such as C26Ci and BJ fibroblasts for IF staining.
Include a negative control using antibody-only stained coverslips containing HCEC cells.
